basis: ESTIMATES. R2 measured a comparable build: W01 core 14.6 min active, 69 tool calls, 217,502 to 433,391 tokens; W02 surface 3.3 min, 16 calls, 113,393 tokens. R5 touches the same two large files with ten interacting repairs and a test-first method, so the child caps are about 5x the R2 W01 figures. Revise by an amended revision after the run.

macro.final_audits_note: none in R5: the audit round is a separate macro pinned to the repaired head with its own operator line

recordable_measures.elapsed: coordinator wall clock at dispatch and return
recordable_measures.advisor_calls: structural count of advisor tool_use/server_tool_use blocks in the child transcript; coordinator calls counted by hand
not_recordable: coordinator's own tokens and active time (UNKNOWN, not budgeted)

on_limit: When ANY limit is reached or about to be exceeded: stop the running child at the next safe point (TaskStop; never mid-commit), dispatch nothing further, retry nothing, substitute nothing, leave the child's edits uncommitted, and report status NEEDS_SUPERVISOR with the allowance, the measured value, the cap and the files touched. A cap changes only by an amended package revision with new hashes and a new operator AUTHORIZE line.
enforcement: Coordinator discipline only (the schemas have no allowance fields; ct validate-macro does not check them). Pinned through each child text, the macro stop-condition and base_policy text, and ALLOWANCES.json by sha256.
closure: At close the coordinator writes ALLOWANCE_LEDGER.json (measured vs cap) into the flat review_bundle; no value is invented.
